title: Consider Holding a Strategic Message Tryout
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This post proposes borrowing the tryout from sports, theater and music as a low-stakes team exercise for sharpening how people communicate the organization's key messages. Without any threat of being cut, the chance to perform in front of peers raises focus and prompts preparation. The suggested format has each person explain the vision, values or strategy in three minutes or less, audience members score clarity and persuasiveness, and the top presenter is celebrated, with video as an optional record. The payoff claimed is that the whole team hears many ways of framing one message, remembers it, and gains alignment and commitment through repetition. It is a concrete, easily piloted idea for leaders who want their messages to stick.
points: Tryouts without elimination energize people because they bring out preparation and peer-visible performance.
Every team member being able to recite and persuasively explain the vision, values and strategy is framed as a core organizational asset.
The format is simple: a three-minute explanation, audience scoring, recognition for the top scorer, and possibly recorded videos.
Hearing a dozen versions of the same message teaches the team varied ways to deliver it and makes it memorable through repetition.
quotes: Absent the threat of being cut from the team, a tryout gets people’s juices flowing. The test of showcasing one’s skills in front of peers and leaders compels team members to bring their best game.

They practice, rehearse, and compete to display to everyone what they are capable of. Anyone who ever played on a sports team, acted in a play, or performed in a band during their school years remembers the elevated focus produced during tryouts. At the end of a tryout, the best performers stand out.

Being able to describe, explain, and persuade others about the key messages of the team and organization is a critical asset for everyone. Ideally, every team member should be able to recite the vision, values, and strategy of the team or organization in a compelling and persuasive way. Asking team members to prepare for a tryout to see who can craft the most cogent presentation for such messages can be highly engaging and entertaining.

Ask everyone in the audience to give each presenter a score reflecting how clear and persuasive the message was. Identify and celebrate the highest-rated presenter. Consider capturing the performances on video so others in the organization can benefit from them.

After a dozen or more presentations, the entire team learns new and diverse ways of delivering the same message more persuasively. One thing is for sure. No one will forget the key message after the Tryout.

Tryouts for touting messages heighten focus, alignment, and commitment. The mild pressure to perform well in front of others encourages everyone to practice and rehearse to be at their best. Are you ready for the Tryout?
